summary: Defines how an IS-IS router advertises supported Maximum SID Depths at node or link level, so controllers can tell whether a given SID stack can be supported in a segment routing network.

eli5.summary: A router says how many labels it can stack, so planners know the limit.

questions: what is base mpls imposition msd
subtitle: How an IS-IS router tells controllers how many segment labels it can push, and the registry of MSD types.

tldr.problem: A controller computing Segment Routing paths must not exceed the SID stack depth a node can impose, but it may have no other way to learn that limit.
tldr.mechanism: IS-IS routers advertise a Node MSD sub-TLV (type 23) in the Router CAPABILITY TLV and a Link MSD sub-TLV (type 15) on link TLVs, each holding pairs of MSD-Type and MSD-Value. The RFC also creates the IGP MSD-Types registry and defines Base MPLS Imposition.
tldr.outcome: Controllers can read node and link limits from IS-IS. A link value overrides the node value, and new MSD-Types can be added through the registry.

today: RFC 8491 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFC. It also defines the IGP MSD-Types registry that RFC 8476 uses for OSPF.

sections.title: Why Routers Advertise MSD
sections.content:
A centralized controller that computes Segment Routing (SR) paths must learn the Maximum SID Depth (MSD) of each node and link, so a computed SID stack is never deeper than the node can impose.

PCEP can signal MSD, but only where it is configured on the head-end. BGP-LS can export it, but usually runs on few nodes. So the RFC says MSD capabilities SHOULD be advertised by every IS-IS router in the network.

The RFC defines the IS-IS extension, creates an IANA registry for MSD-Type identifiers and defines one type, Base MPLS Imposition. MSD may also be useful when SR is not enabled: in a non-SR MPLS network it defines the maximum label depth.
sections.eli5: The planner needs to know how many labels each router can carry. Routers announce their limit so the planner can stay within it.

sections.title: Key Terms: MSD, SID and Imposition
sections.content:
MSD is the number of SIDs supported by a node or a link on a node. Label imposition is modifying or adding labels to a packet's outgoing label stack, by replacing the top label or pushing new ones. The number imposed is the replaced labels plus the pushed ones.

BMI, Base MPLS Imposition, is the number of MPLS labels that can be imposed, inclusive of all service, transport and special labels.
sections.eli5: Imposition is putting stickers on a package. BMI counts every sticker of every kind.

sections.title: The Node MSD Sub-TLV
sections.content:
The Node MSD sub-TLV goes in the IS-IS Router CAPABILITY TLV from RFC 7981. It carries the provisioned SID depth of the originating router. Node MSD is the smallest MSD supported by the node on the interfaces configured for the advertising IGP instance. Values may come from a hardware API or be provisioned.

It is Type 23. Length is a multiple of 2 octets. The value is one or more pairs of a 1-octet MSD-Type and a 1-octet MSD-Value. MSD-Value is 0 to 255; 0 means no ability to support a SID stack of any depth, and any other value MUST be the lowest value supported by any link configured for use by the IS-IS instance.

The sub-TLV is optional. If a router originates several Node MSD advertisements for the same MSD-Type, the procedures of RFC 7981 apply. This may result in different values being used by different controllers, which the RFC says causes no interoperability issue.
sections.eli5: The router writes down pairs: what kind of limit, and the number. It can write several pairs.

sections.title: The Link MSD Sub-TLV
sections.content:
The Link MSD sub-TLV carries the MSD of the interface for a link. It is defined for TLVs 22, 23, 25, 141, 222 and 223, has Type 15, and uses the same pairs of MSD-Type and MSD-Value. Values may be signaled by the forwarding plane or provisioned. A nonzero value is that of the link when used as an outgoing interface.

The sub-TLV is optional. If several Link MSD advertisements for the same MSD-Type and link are received, which copy to use is undefined.

If the router imposes labels in the context of the ingress interface, a per-link value cannot be meaningful. In that case only the Node MSD SHOULD be advertised.
sections.eli5: A router can also give a limit for each road out of it, unless the limit depends on which road the packet came in on.

sections.title: Combining Node and Link Values
sections.content:
A Link MSD for an MSD-Type MUST take precedence over the Node MSD. If only the Node MSD is signaled, it MUST be used for the link. To increase flooding efficiency, routers with the same MSD on every link are RECOMMENDED to advertise just the Node MSD.

If neither is advertised for a type, generally it only means the node does not support advertising that type. In some cases it might mean the function is not supported. The correct interpretation MUST be specified when an MSD-Type is defined.
sections.eli5: A rule for one road beats the rule for the whole router. If every road is the same, one note is enough.

sections.title: Base MPLS Imposition MSD
sections.content:
The one MSD-Type defined here is Base MPLS Imposition MSD (BMI-MSD). It signals the total number of MPLS labels that can be imposed, including all service, transport and special labels.

If BMI-MSD is not advertised, that indicates only that the node does not support advertising this capability.
sections.eli5: This is the total count of labels of every kind a router can put on a packet.

sections.title: IANA Registry and Assignments
sections.content:
IANA allocated sub-TLV 23 (Node MSD) in the registry for sub-TLVs of TLV 242, and sub-TLV 15 (Link MSD) in the registry for sub-TLVs of TLVs 22, 23, 25, 141, 222 and 223.

IANA also created the IGP MSD-Types registry. The procedure is Expert Review per RFC 8126, and types are unsigned 8-bit numbers. Value 0 is reserved, 1 is Base MPLS Imposition MSD, 2 to 250 are unassigned, 251 to 254 are for experimental use, and 255 is reserved.
sections.eli5: There is now an official list of limit kinds with numbers. Kind 1 is the total label count.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security considerations of RFC 7981 apply. A wrong MSD has consequences. A value that is too small may make path computation fail to find a viable path. A value that is too large may lead to an attempt to build a path the head-end cannot support. The information may also tell an attacker how to induce these conditions.
sections.eli5: A wrong number can make the planner give up or ask for too much, and a bad guy who sees the numbers could take advantage.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Multiple of 2 octets; total length of the value field.

fields.name: MSD-Type
fields.desc: Kind of MSD, from the IGP MSD-Types registry.

fields.name: MSD-Value
fields.desc: 0 to 255; 0 means no ability to support a stack.

items.label: Base MPLS Imposition MSD
items.desc: Total MPLS labels that can be imposed.
